checked_non_problem_annotations.locator: Theorem 2.3, Definition 2.4, Lemma 2.5 and Remark 2.6, pp7-9
checked_non_problem_annotations.target: Archimedean normalization connecting level-set counts to the prime integral
checked_non_problem_annotations.status: Explicit inconsistency verified; correction and its local effect derived
checked_non_problem_annotations.assumptions: F homogeneous of positive degree d on R^D; Omega a nice compact positive-measure subset of F=1. In the checked concrete example F=det on Mat_2, D=4,d=2.
logic: Write C=[0,1]Omega and V_C=vol_D(C). Homogeneity of Lebesgue volume gives vol([1-epsilon,1+epsilon]Omega)=((1+epsilon)^D-(1-epsilon)^D)V_C. Thus the displayed radial-shell definition gives mu_rad(Omega)=D V_C.
For the F-level coarea measure mu_F(Omega)=integral_Omega |grad F|^{-1}dS, scaling the level F=r gives mu_F(r^{1/d}Omega)=r^{D/d-1}mu_F(Omega). Therefore V_C=(d/D)mu_F(Omega), and mu_rad=d mu_F.

For large T, I(T)=integral_{T Omega}1/log^+(F(x))dx=mu_F(Omega) integral_0^{T^d} r^{D/d-1}/max(2,log r)dr. Hence I(T)~mu_F(Omega)T^D/(D log T)=mu_rad(Omega)T^D/(d D log T). The compact initial range of r contributes O(1).

Lemma 2.5 uses mu_rad by the preceding displayed definition but prints mu_rad T^D/(D log T), missing the factor 1/d. The first coarea equality in its proof integrates r from 1-epsilon to 1+epsilon, which corresponds to radial endpoints (1-epsilon)^(1/d),(1+epsilon)^(1/d), not [1-epsilon,1+epsilon].

Concrete patch: Omega={(a,b;c,(1+bc)/a):1<=a<=2,0<=b<=1,0<=c<=1}. It is a compact connected 3-dimensional graph in det=1 with finite smooth boundary pieces; the boundary has surface measure zero. Because partial(det)/partial(x22)=a, coarea gives dmu_F=da db dc/a on this graph. Thus mu_F=log 2, mu_rad=2 log 2, and V_C=(log 2)/2.

For this patch, the actual prime integral coefficient is (log 2)/4 multiplying T^4/log T. Lemma 2.5 with its explicit radial-shell definition instead gives (log 2)/2. This is a factor-two contradiction to that literal normalization, not a prime-distribution assumption.
checked_non_problem_annotations.repair: Define mu_infinity by the F-level shell: lim_{epsilon->0} vol([(1-epsilon)^(1/d),(1+epsilon)^(1/d)]Omega)/(2epsilon), or divide the displayed radial-shell definition by d. Then Remark 2.6 and the asserted integral asymptotic agree.
checked_non_problem_annotations.counterevidence_and_limit: Remark 2.6 already explicitly uses the coarea normalization, and the later cone computation is consistent with that corrected normalization. Therefore this check establishes an inconsistent intermediate definition/proof, not falsity of Theorems 1.4, 1.6 or 1.8. The exact normalization in the external Oh/Borovoi-Rudnick sources was not fetched or independently certified.

checked_non_problem_annotations.target: Local density stability and local obstructions for determinant prime levels
checked_non_problem_annotations.status: Corrected local stability checked analytically, including an exact formula
checked_non_problem_annotations.assumptions: n>=2; prime target p; q denotes a place; source local density denominator q^{k(n^2-1)}.
logic: For q not dividing m, left multiplication by diag(u,1,...,1), with u a unit modulo q^k, bijects determinant fibers with values differing by the unit u. The determinant map is smooth at an invertible matrix, so each solution modulo q lifts to q^{(k-1)(n^2-1)} solutions of a fixed unit determinant modulo q^k.

The normalized unit density is beta_q=q^{-(n^2-1)}#SL_n(F_q)=product_{j=2}^n(1-q^{-j}). Counting independent ordered columns gives #GL_n(F_q)=product_{i=0}^{n-1}(q^n-q^i), and dividing by q-1 counts each nonzero determinant fiber.

The displayed equalities on pp10-11 omit q^{-(n^2-1)} from #GL_n(F_q)/(q-1). For n=2,q=2 and any odd target p, the actual normalized density is 6/8=3/4, whereas the printed right side is 6. The correctly normalized Bateman-Horn Euler factor was already printed on p9.

At q=p with target determinant exactly p mod p^k, a mod-p matrix of rank <=n-2 cannot contribute for k>=2: every lift has at least two p-divisible Smith invariant factors, hence determinant divisible by p^2. Rank n-1 matrices are nonsingular points of det=0 and each contributes p^{(k-1)(n^2-1)} lifts with the specified determinant.

The number of rank n-1 matrices over F_p is [(p^n-1)/(p-1)] product_{i=0}^{n-2}(p^n-p^i): choose a one-dimensional kernel, then an injective map from the (n-1)-dimensional quotient into F_p^n. Dividing this count by p^{n^2-1} gives delta_p=beta_p(1+p^{-1}+...+p^{-(n-1)}).

Consequently, with the corrected normalization, S_p=S_det(1+p^{-1}+...+p^{-(n-1)}). This proves the required stability with O(p^{-1}), stronger than the printed O(p^{-1/2}), without using an uninspected Lang-Weil reference.

There is no fixed-prime local obstruction for the determinant family: diag(m,1,...,1) realizes every integer m. The convergent product S_det=product_{j=2}^n zeta(j)^{-1} is positive, since the local deviations are O(q^{-2}).
checked_non_problem_annotations.correction: Insert q^{-(n^2-1)} in both displayed normalized unit-density identities on pp10-11. The exact rank-count calculation supplies a direct check of the bad-place stability used in the prime sum.
checked_non_problem_annotations.limits: This is a local count, not a new proof of the homogeneous-dynamics equidistribution theorem or an unconditional certification of the global theorem. It concerns the integer matrix lattice with the usual coordinate volume.

checked_non_problem_annotations.locator: Theorem 3.2 to Theorem 3.1, pp9-12; comparison with p13
checked_non_problem_annotations.target: Legitimacy and normalization of the prime-level summation
hypotheses_used: Use the coarea-normalized mu_F from C0388-A.
Assume the external level-count input as stated in Theorem 3.2 with that normalization: N(m,Omega)=mu_F(Omega)m^{n-1}S_m(1+r_m), r_m->0 for each fixed Omega.
Use the exact local stability verified in C0388-B.
Use the ordinary prime number theorem as an external standard input, not proved or fetched in this task.
logic: For fixed Omega, compactness makes every fixed small-prime contribution finite. For any eta>0 choose M so that |r_m|<=eta for all m>=M. Split the prime sum at M: the finite head is O_Omega,M(1), and the tail error is at most eta times the positive main weighted sum. Thus summing the pointwise m-asymptotic is valid; no unproved uniformity over varying Omega is needed for this fixed-cone step.

Partial summation from pi(Y)~Y/log Y gives sum_{p<=Y}p^a~Y^{a+1}/((a+1)log Y) for fixed a>=0. The identity is Y^a pi(Y)-a integral_2^Y t^{a-1}pi(t)dt; subtracting the leading integrals yields the factor 1/(a+1).

Set Y=T^n and a=n-1. Then sum_{p<=T^n}p^{n-1}~T^{n^2}/(n^2 log T). The source's p11 third line has T^n, an inconsistent exponent; the surrounding weighted sum and following coarea formula require T^{n^2}.

The density error O(p^{-1}) from the exact formula, or the weaker source O(p^{-1/2}), contributes o(T^{n^2}/log T). For n>=2 this follows directly by bounding the smaller-power prime sum; the finite initial primes again have bounded contribution.
Thus the corrected conditional determinant cone count is mu_F(Omega)S_det T^{n^2}/(n^2 log T)(1+o(1)), exactly S_det times the correctly normalized coarea prime integral.
For the Pfaffian dimension D=n(2n-1) and degree d=n, the corresponding exponent a=D/d-1=2n-2 gives T^{n(2n-1)}/[n(2n-1)log T]. The p13 prime-sum coefficient is correct.
boundary_checks: Only positive levels enter these cones in F=1. Negative-prime/prime-ideal conclusions require a separate negative-level argument; they are not silently inferred here.
The origin and F=0 have no positive-prime contribution. The small range of F where log^+ differs from log contributes O(1) for a fixed compact cone.
The Omega boundary has surface measure zero as required by the external equidistribution input. The explicit test patch satisfies this condition.

An epsilon-cutting may use finitely many cones at each fixed epsilon; pointwise-in-Omega errors may be summed for that fixed finite collection. This does not validate the construction or exceptional-region sieve in Sections 4-5.
No interchange of T->infinity and epsilon->0 was certified here beyond the fixed-cone argument.
checked_non_problem_annotations.limits: Conditional on the cited level-set equidistribution theorem and ordinary PNT. No fresh proof or external validation of Oh's theorem is claimed.

checked_non_problem_annotations.target: Pfaffian fiber dimension and a local normalization boundary case
checked_non_problem_annotations.status: Wrong denominator proved to yield divergent local factors; direct repair checked
logic: The lattice of alternating 2n by 2n matrices has D=binom(2n,2)=2n^2-n independent coordinates. A nonsingular fixed-Pfaffian fiber has dimension D-1, so its counting density must use q^{k(D-1)}.

Theorem 3.5 instead prints q^{k(n^2-1)}. For n=2, write the six independent entries as a,b,c,d,e,f with Pfaffian af-be+cd. Over F_q, the equation Pf=1 has exactly (q^3-1)q^2 solutions: choose nonzero (a,b,c), then solve the nonzero linear equation in (f,-e,d).
Every Pf=1 point is smooth because a gradient vector could vanish only if all six entries vanished, impossible on that fiber. Hence the number modulo q^k is (q^3-1)q^2 q^{5(k-1)}.

For q=3 the correctly normalized density is 26/27. Dividing by the printed q^{3k} instead of q^{5k} gives (26/27)3^{2k}, which diverges. This is an explicit local calculation for n=2 in the theorem's allowed range, with no appeal to unseen literature.
The correction is q^{k(2n^2-n-1)}, agreeing with the general q^{k dim(V_m)} normalization on p7 and with the m^{2n-2} exponent already printed in Theorem 3.5.
The source's diagonal-congruence map scales the Pfaffian by the unit b, not b^2: each monomial uses the first index exactly once. This validates the unit-fiber bijection at the algebraic level.
Block diagonal matrices diag(mJ,J,...,J), J=[[0,1],[-1,0]], realize every integer m as Pfaffian, so there is no fixed-prime obstruction in the integral alternating lattice.
checked_non_problem_annotations.counterevidence: The ambient dimension and general density definition determine an explicit correction. Together with the dimensionally correct p13 weighted prime sum, this supports interpreting the denominator as a local copied formula error rather than evidence that the final Pfaffian asymptotic is false.
checked_non_problem_annotations.limits: The full general-n finite-field count attributed to MacWilliams and the external Pfaffian Linnik theorem were read as citations only, not fetched or independently reproved. Over characteristic two, the check uses the base change of the integral alternating lattice (zero diagonal), not the larger set obtained by imposing only A^T=-A over F_2.

checked_non_problem_annotations.target: Signature restrictions and the two distinct uses of parity
logic: For a nonsingular real symmetric matrix with negative index v, sign(det)=(-1)^v. Thus det=1 and positive-prime cones admit only even v. The statement that V_1 has n+1 signature orbits is not literally correct; V_1 contains floor(n/2)+1 such signatures.

The indicator psi(u,v)=1 for v even and zero otherwise is consistent with positive-prime counting. For odd v, log^+(det)=infinity and the positive-prime integral vanishes; a negative-prime statement requires the separate det=-1 side.

The Hasse invariant of a real form is (-1)^{v(v-1)/2}; for admissible even v it reduces to (-1)^{v/2}. The finite matching condition can therefore still change with signature even after determinant sign is fixed.
The factor 2 from the adelic density in Corollary 7.3 is different from the one-half prime-place local mass in Proposition 7.4. Multiplying them cancels these factors for both odd and even rank.

This verifies sign bookkeeping and the product of stated factors. It does not reprove that every indicated 2-adic orbit has exactly one matching prime-place orbit; that classification remains an explicitly unverified input.
checked_non_problem_annotations.limits: No extension to negative-prime counts is inferred solely from this positive-level computation.

checked_non_problem_annotations.target: Low-rank precision of the prime-dividing-determinant density
checked_non_problem_annotations.status: Internal formula inconsistency verified; weaker sufficient error identified
logic: Let n=2r+1 be odd and ell an odd prime. The Jordan blocks have ranks 2r and 1. Write chi=(((-1)^r det(f0))/ell), which is plus or minus one because f0 is unimodular.
Substitution in the displayed equation (11) gives alpha_ell(S)^-1=(1/(2ell))(1-chi ell^-r)^-1 product_{i=1}^{r-1}(1-ell^-2i)^-1.
The displayed standard factor is alpha_std^-1=product_{i=1}^{r}(1-ell^-2i)^-1. Hence the exact relative ratio from those displayed formulas is 1+chi ell^-r.

For n=3 choose the positive-definite integral matrix S=diag(1,1,ell), of determinant ell. Then chi=(-1/ell), and the relative ratio is exactly 1+chi/ell, which is not 1+O(ell^-2). Thus Lemma 6.2's uniform n>=3 relative precision is incompatible with equation (11).

For odd n>=5 the exponent r>=2 makes the stated O(ell^-2) sufficient. For even n=2r, f0 has odd rank 2r-1 and the same substitution gives the stated leading factor exactly, with no analogous rank-three exception.

Replacing the uniform assertion by 1+O(ell^-1), or treating n=3 separately, is enough for the prime asymptotics. Proposition 7.4 already states O(ell^-1), and p32's class-number calculation explicitly uses O(ell^-1).
checked_non_problem_annotations.counterevidence: The required o(1) stability and weighted prime sums survive the weaker error. No final symmetric-matrix prime-counting theorem is refuted by this discrepancy.
checked_non_problem_annotations.external_limit: The algebra is derived from the manuscript's stated equation (11). The external Conway-Sloane mass formula itself was not accessed or independently certified.

checked_non_problem_annotations.target: Exact direct rank-four 2-adic density, without assuming a mass formula
checked_non_problem_annotations.status: Analytical derivation plus actual exhaustive finite calculation
analytic_derivation: Enumerate Sym_4(F_2): the actual own-script count finds 448 invertible matrices, of which 28 are alternating and 420 nonalternating. The rank calculation is exact binary Gaussian elimination over all 2^10 independent-entry choices.

For a nonalternating invertible symmetric matrix modulo 2, its inverse is also nonalternating: otherwise x^T A^-1 x=0 for all x, and setting x=Ay would force y^T Ay=0 for all y. Therefore some diagonal cofactor is odd. The determinant has a unit partial derivative in a diagonal coordinate, so each fixed odd determinant fiber has 2^9 lifts at each step. Its normalized Type-I contribution is 420/2^9=105/128, independent of the odd target.

Every invertible alternating matrix modulo 2 is congruent to H=diag(J,J), J=[[0,1],[1,0]]. A lift of the congruence matrix to GL_4(Z/8Z) has odd determinant, whose square is 1 modulo 8, so congruence preserves the target determinant residue modulo 8. All 28 alternating residue classes therefore have the same lift counts.
Write S=H+2B. Since det(H)=1 and H^-1=H, expanding det(I+2HB) modulo 8 gives 1+2 tr(HB)+4 e_2(HB). For symmetric B this simplifies to det(S)=1+4(B11 B22+B33 B44) modulo 8.

The formula depends only on B modulo 2. Each diagonal pair has three choices with product zero and one with product one; equal products occur in 3*3+1*1=10 of 16 diagonal choices, and unequal products in 6. The six independent off-diagonal bits are free, giving 640 binary B with determinant 1 modulo 8 and 384 with determinant 5. The script checks the formula against exact signed-permutation determinants for all 1024 B.

Each binary B has 2^10 extensions modulo 4. Thus the Type-II counts modulo 8 are 28*2^10*640 and 28*2^10*384 for target residues 1 and 5; residues 3 and 7 receive no Type-II contribution. Dividing by 8^9 gives 35/256 and 21/256.

These mod-8 densities stabilize. For any invertible alternating reduction choose an off-diagonal cofactor that is odd; the symmetric-coordinate derivative of det is twice that cofactor. For k>=3, perturb that coordinate by 2^{k-1}. This preserves det modulo 2^k and flips its next bit modulo 2^{k+1}; the quadratic remainder is divisible by 2^{2k-2}, hence by 2^{k+1}. The perturbation pairs solutions modulo 2^k into the two possible next determinant bits.

For Type II all determinant partial derivatives are even, so all 2^10 lifts of a matrix modulo 2^k have the same determinant modulo 2^{k+1}. Exactly half of the solutions at level k lift to the specified next bit; hence N_{k+1}=2^9 N_k and the normalized density is constant from k=3 onward.
Adding Type I yields total fixed-unit densities delta_2(a): 245/256 for a=1, 105/128 for a=3, 231/256 for a=5, and 105/128 for a=7 modulo 8.

Their mean is 7/8. Independently, the directly counted Bateman-Horn factor at 2 is (448/1024)/(1-1/2)=7/8. This verifies the local normalization and the aggregate residue-class matching in this lowest even-rank case.

checked_non_problem_annotations.target: Even-rank L-series averaging and final prime-density cancellation
checked_non_problem_annotations.status: Conditional leading-asymptotic deduction checked, with a fixed-cutoff argument

notation.odd_zeta_product: S_n=product over odd j, 3<=j<=n, of zeta(j)^-1
notation.L_convention: L_odd(r,chi_ell)=sum over odd m with (m,ell)=1 of (((-1)^r ell)/m)m^{-r}; the Euler factor at 2 is omitted.

logic: The p20 convention sets the local Legendre symbol to zero when the place divides 2D, and p30 explicitly expands only odd m. Thus the final cancellation is checked using L_odd. Replacing this by a primitive L-function with a nontrivial factor at 2 without compensating the branch constants would change the calculation; no such replacement is made.

For each fixed odd nonsquare m, the Jacobi symbol as a function of the prime ell is a nonprincipal character modulo an odd divisor of m. Restricting ell to one reduced residue class modulo 8 does not trivialize it, by the Chinese remainder theorem. The prime number theorem in fixed arithmetic progressions therefore gives a zero weighted mean for this term.
For m=t^2 with t odd, the character is one except at primes dividing t, whose contribution for fixed t is finite. The square coefficients sum to sum_{t odd}t^{-n}=(1-2^{-n})zeta(n).

The exchange of summation and limiting mean can be justified with a fixed cutoff M: for r>=2 the absolute tail is bounded uniformly in ell by sum_{m>M}m^{-r}, which tends to zero. For the finite head use only fixed-modulus prime number theorems, then let M tend to infinity. This proves the leading o(1) mean without claiming the source's uniform log^{-101} estimates were externally verified.
Consequently, for each a0 modulo 8 with gcd(a0,8)=1, sum_{ell<=T^n,ell=a0 mod8} L_odd(r,chi_ell)ell^{(n-1)/2} ~ [(1-2^{-n})zeta(n)/4] A(T).

The three branch multipliers from the corrected equations (16)-(18) are C0=1 if ell is not congruent to epsilon modulo4; Cplus=1+2^{1-n}/(1-x) if ell=epsilon modulo4 and ell=plus/minus1 modulo8; Cminus=1+2^{1-n}/(1+x) for the remaining eligible class. There are respectively two, one and one reduced residue classes, for either parity of r.
The class-weighted multiplier is (1-x^2)[1/2+(1/4)(1+2x^2/(1-x))+(1/4)(1+2x^2/(1+x))]=1. Indeed the bracket equals 1+x^2/(1-x^2)=1/(1-x^2).

Multiplying Corollary 7.3's factor 2 by Proposition 7.4's one-half leaves no extra one-half. With that correction, the odd-zeta product S_n remains and the averaged cone count is psi(u,v) mu_F(Omega) S_n A(T)(1+o(1)), agreeing with the coarea prime integral.
local_discrepancies: Proposition 7.4's final even-rank branch on p24 must read 1+2^{1-n}/(1+2^{-n/2}), as in equation (18), rather than the printed minus sign and minus denominator.
The extra one-half in the even-rank prime sum on p29 must be removed; p30's final calculation already uses the corrected cancellation.

The displayed statements of Lemmas 7.5 and 7.7 omit the odd-zeta product that is present in their preceding derivations. This was visually confirmed and is a local formula omission, not a new density counterexample.

checked_non_problem_annotations.status: Algebraic matching verified conditional on the displayed input formulas
logic: For odd n, Proposition 7.11 supplies ell^{(n-1)/2} pi^{-n(n+1)/4} product Gamma(k/2) times all even zeta factors up to n-1. Lemma 7.13 supplies the reciprocal gamma and pi factors and product_{j=2}^n zeta(j)^-1. All even zeta factors cancel, leaving mu_F(Omega) ell^{(n-1)/2} S_n.

For even n, the class-number branch factors are 2 C0, 2 Cplus, 2 Cminus. The extra one-half in Lemma 7.13 cancels the leading 2. The even zeta factors through n-2 cancel, leaving zeta(n)^-1 L_odd(r,chi_ell) C_a S_n multiplied by ell^{(n-1)/2} mu_F(Omega).
This is the same prime-level expression as in the corrected indefinite calculation, so the fixed-cutoff averaging from SYM0388-D yields the same S_n leading constant.

The first N(p,Omega) display on p36 omits p^{(n-1)/2}; that factor is visibly present in Proposition 7.11 and required by the following application of Lemma 7.6. Restoring it reconciles the local displayed formula with the subsequent correctly scaled count.

The parity explanation c_n=1 for odd n and 2 for even n is consistent with the generic central stabilizer inside SL_n, where -I belongs to SL_n precisely for even n. The absolute quotient volumes and differential-form conversion were cited external inputs and were not independently rederived.
checked_non_problem_annotations.limits: This checks multiplication and cancellation of the displayed class-number and measure formulas. It does not certify EMMV genus equidistribution, Kitaoka's theorem, their precise quoted hypotheses, the all-rank mass calculation, or Zhang/DRS absolute measure normalization.

V=R^2,F=x therefore qualifies. R0={0<=x<=1/2,|y|<=x} is compact, convex and star-shaped, with area integral_0^(1/2)2x dx=1/4. Its radial intersection with F=1 is the compact segment (1,s), |s|<=1, with boundary of measure zero on V1. In the exact union required by Definition 4.4 every cone piece must be contained in R0. Any nonempty Omega consequently lies in that radial segment and has L-infinity height 1. Its required [0,1/height] cone contains Omega itself at x=1, outside R0. Thus no nonempty piece is possible, and the empty collection leaves an exceptional set of area 1/4 for every epsilon<1/4. independent_subchecks.item: Determinant unit fibers and prime powers
independent_subchecks.reasoning: A unit determinant fiber over Fq has #GL_n(Fq)/(q-1) elements, and each lifts by q^(n^2-1) at every next level. Thus the normalized density is q^-(n^2-1)#GL_n/(q-1)=product_(j=2)^n(1-q^-j). The two displayed equalities on pages 10-11 omit that power. At n=q=2 this is 6/8=3/4, whereas the printed right side is 6. Also, weighted prime summation gives sum_(p<=T^n)p^(n-1)~T^(n^2)/(n^2 log T), not the T^n numerator printed on page 11.

The integral alternating 2n-by-2n lattice has D=2n^2-n independent coordinates; a unit Pfaffian fiber has dimension D-1. For n=2, Pf=af-be+cd, so over Fq exactly (q^3-1)q^2 tuples give 1: choose a nonzero first triple and solve one nonzero linear equation in the second. Every such point is smooth, giving q^(5(k-1)) lifts. At q=3 the correct density is 26/27, while the page-12 denominator q^(k(n^2-1))=3^(3k) gives (26/27)3^(2k). The repair q^(k(2n^2-n-1)) agrees with the general page-7 definition and the correct page-13 weighted-prime exponent. This calculation uses the alternating integer lattice with zero diagonal, including after reduction at 2.

For S=diag(1,1,p), the page-21 formula (11) gives alpha_p^-1=[2p(1-chi/p)]^-1, chi=(-1/p). The standard odd-rank factor from (10) is (1-p^-2)^-1. Their relative ratio after the stated (2p)^-1 prefactor is (1-p^-2)/(1-chi/p)=1+chi/p, not 1+O(p^-2). The weaker O(p^-1) is sufficient, and is explicitly used on page 32. This is an internal substitution in the quoted formula, not a new verification of the external mass theorem.

The final branch of Proposition 7.4 must agree with equation (18): 1+2^(1-n)/(1+2^(-n/2)). Its printed minus/minus expression disagrees. Corollary 7.3 contributes factor 2, cancelling Proposition 7.4's 1/2, so the extra 1/2 on page 29 is absent from the correct product. Multiplying the class-number formula on page 32 by Lemma 7.13's measure formula restores p^((n-1)/2) in the first page-36 display. The odd zeta factors present in the preceding derivations must remain in Lemmas 7.5 and 7.7. Gamma and pi factors cancel, even zetas cancel through n-1 in odd rank and n-2 in even rank, and the parity factor 1/2 in even rank cancels the leading class-number 2.
